display.title: Counting the Omer: Every Day Is Precious (The Lost Dime)
display.summary_short: Why we count each day of Sefirah: every day should be better than the one before, and time, Hashem's gift, can never be bought back, as a girl who lost a dime learns.
display.summary_long: A talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show during Sefiras HaOmer. Uncle Yossi asks why we make a brachah just to count days, and explains that each day counts higher than the one before to show that today must be better than yesterday. Time cannot be bought, stopped or recovered once it is lost. He tells of a little girl named Miriam who keeps crying over a lost dime even as her mother gives her new ones, until her mother explains that she must stop mourning the first dime and simply take care of the ones she has now. Like a person who lovingly counts his jewels, we count our days and fill each one with Torah and mitzvos, and Hashem rewards this with long life, as we say in the second paragraph of the Shema.
display.lesson: Time is a precious gift from Hashem: don't waste it or dwell on what was lost, and make each day better than the one before.
